name: Sellsy
description: Sellsy, the French CRM and invoicing suite: companies, individuals and contacts, opportunities and pipelines, estimates, orders, invoices, credit notes, payments, catalogue items, tasks, comments and calendar events, with search, creates and edits. REST API v2, OAuth 2.0 client credentials.
instructions:
## Sellsy
This connector calls the **Sellsy API v2** (`https://api.sellsy.com/v2`), the French CRM and invoicing suite: companies, individuals and contacts, opportunities and pipelines, estimates, orders, deliveries, invoices, credit notes, payments, the item catalogue, tasks, comments, calendar events, staff, files and subscriptions.

**Getting credentials**
1. Sign in to Sellsy, open **Settings, API** (Paramètres, API) and create an **application** in the developer area.
2. Choose the *client credentials* flow: it authorises the application against your own account with no browser consent step. You receive a **client id** and **client secret**.
3. Give the application the scopes it needs: read access for the areas you want to query (companies, contacts, individuals, opportunities, estimates, invoices, credit-notes, orders, deliveries, payments, items, taxes, tasks, comments, calendars, activities, staffs, files, custom-fields, subscriptions, search, accounts) and write access only where the AI should create or change records.
4. Set `SELLSY_CLIENT_ID` and `SELLSY_CLIENT_SECRET`. AnythingMCP mints and refreshes the access token on its own.

**This is API v2**, at `https://api.sellsy.com/v2`. Sellsy's v1 was an entirely different, single-endpoint RPC API: if you find an example that POSTs everything to one URL with a `request` parameter, that is v1 and it does not apply here.

**Workflow**
- Find anything by text first: `sellsy_search` (like the search bar; narrow with `type`).
- Companies: `sellsy_list_companies`, `sellsy_search_companies`, `sellsy_get_company`, `sellsy_create_company`, `sellsy_edit_company`; their people with `sellsy_list_company_contacts`, `sellsy_link_contact_to_company`; addresses with `sellsy_list_company_addresses`, `sellsy_create_company_address`; custom fields with `sellsy_get_company_custom_fields`, `sellsy_update_company_custom_fields`; attachments with `sellsy_list_company_files` and `sellsy_get_file`.
- Contacts (people at companies): `sellsy_list_contacts`, `sellsy_search_contacts`, `sellsy_get_contact`, `sellsy_list_contact_companies`, `sellsy_create_contact`, `sellsy_edit_contact`.
- Individuals (private customers, a separate object from contacts): `sellsy_list_individuals`, `sellsy_search_individuals`, `sellsy_get_individual`, `sellsy_create_individual`, `sellsy_edit_individual`.
- Pipeline: `sellsy_list_opportunities`, `sellsy_search_opportunities`, `sellsy_get_opportunity`; set-up data from `sellsy_list_opportunity_pipelines`, `sellsy_list_pipeline_steps`, `sellsy_list_opportunity_sources`, `sellsy_list_opportunity_categories`; changes with `sellsy_create_opportunity`, `sellsy_update_opportunity`, `sellsy_move_opportunity_step`. `sellsy_update_opportunity` is a partial update: list every field you send in `only`.
- Sales documents: estimates with `sellsy_list_estimates`, `sellsy_search_estimates`, `sellsy_get_estimate`, `sellsy_create_estimate`, `sellsy_update_estimate_status`; orders and deliveries with `sellsy_list_orders`, `sellsy_search_orders`, `sellsy_get_order`, `sellsy_list_deliveries`; invoices with `sellsy_list_invoices`, `sellsy_search_invoices`, `sellsy_get_invoice`, `sellsy_create_invoice`, `sellsy_validate_invoice`, `sellsy_list_invoice_payments`, `sellsy_list_invoice_credit_notes`, `sellsy_list_invoice_files`; credit notes with `sellsy_list_credit_notes`, `sellsy_search_credit_notes`, `sellsy_get_credit_note`.
- Money in: `sellsy_list_payments`, `sellsy_search_payments`, `sellsy_get_payment`, `sellsy_list_payment_methods`. Recurring invoicing: `sellsy_list_subscriptions`, `sellsy_get_subscription` (open beta at Sellsy).
- Catalogue: `sellsy_list_items`, `sellsy_search_items`, `sellsy_get_item`, `sellsy_get_item_prices`, `sellsy_create_item`, `sellsy_edit_item`; reference data for documents with `sellsy_list_taxes`, `sellsy_list_units`, `sellsy_list_currencies`, `sellsy_list_payment_terms`, `sellsy_list_rate_categories`.
- Follow-up: tasks with `sellsy_list_tasks`, `sellsy_search_tasks`, `sellsy_get_task`, `sellsy_create_task`, `sellsy_update_task`, `sellsy_list_task_labels`; notes with `sellsy_list_comments`, `sellsy_search_comments`, `sellsy_create_comment`; meetings with `sellsy_list_calendar_events`, `sellsy_search_calendar_events`, `sellsy_get_calendar_event`, `sellsy_create_calendar_event`, `sellsy_update_calendar_event`, `sellsy_list_calendar_event_labels`; the activity feed with `sellsy_list_crm_activity`.
- People and set-up: `sellsy_list_staffs`, `sellsy_get_staff`, `sellsy_list_teams`, `sellsy_list_custom_fields`, `sellsy_get_quotas`.

**Searching is a POST.** Sellsy's v2 list endpoints have a sibling `/search` that takes a JSON body of `{"filters": {...}}`. It is far more expressive than the query parameters on the plain list, which is why the search tools are POSTs that only read.

**Sellsy validates every argument against its spec.** `order`, `direction` and `embed` accept only the listed values, and the search filters reject unknown keys (`ids`, `updated` on companies) and bare dates where a date-time is expected (`created.start` must be `2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00`, not `2026-01-01`; the document `date` filters on estimates and invoices take plain dates). A 400 "invalid arguments" almost always means one of these.

**`embed` resolves relationships.** A document returns its `related` parties as ids; `embed[]=contact` and similar bring them back inline and save a round of calls. Each endpoint has its own list of allowed embeds; `cf.<id>` adds a custom field.

**Linking records**: tasks, comments and events take `related` as `[{"type": "company", "id": 123}]` (one record); documents take `related` with one client company or individual and optional contact and opportunities. Ids are integers. Staff ids (`owner_id`, `assigned_staff_ids`) come from `sellsy_list_staffs`; `sellsy_get_staff` with `me` is the API user.

**Paging**: `limit` (max 100, default 25) and `offset`, where `offset` is the opaque `pagination.offset` token of the previous response; `pagination.total` is the number of matches.

**Amounts are strings in the document's currency**, with the tax detail in a separate `amounts` object. `total_amount_without_taxes` and `total_amount` are both present, and confusing them is how a revenue figure ends up 20% wrong. Invoice statuses: draft, due, payinprogress, paid, late, cancelled. Dates are ISO 8601; document dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

**Writes** change the live CRM and accounting: confirm each one with the user first and send only the fields that change. Created estimates and invoices start as drafts; `sellsy_validate_invoice` gives an invoice its final number and cannot be undone, and under French e-invoicing rules may transmit it. The Sellsy application needs the matching write scopes; with read-only rights a write answers 403. Orders and deliveries also answer 403 when the account plan or the application scopes do not include them; the other documents keep working.

**Limits and errors**: Sellsy applies per-account API quotas (`sellsy_get_quotas`); a 429 means wait and retry. Errors come as `{"error": {"code", "message", "context", "details"}}`, where `details` names the field that was refused. 401: the client id or secret is wrong or the application was deleted. 403: a scope is missing. 404: the id does not exist in this account.

**Cloud reachability**: api.sellsy.com is public with a valid certificate.

**Switched off at install**: `sellsy_validate_invoice`, because a validated invoice gets its final number and can no longer be edited or deleted; an admin switches it on when the team needs it.

tools.name: sellsy_list_companies
tools.description: List client companies with their name, SIRET, VAT number, address and owner. The quickest call for checking the OAuth client works.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2…) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: invoicing_address, delivery_address, e_invoicing, main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact, opportunities, estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, acl, smart_tags, owner, or cf.<customFieldId>. Any other value is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_search_companies
tools.description: Search companies with Sellsy's filter object (a POST that only reads). Only the documented filter keys are accepted; an unknown key or a bare date is a 400.

filters.description: Sellsy company filters. ONLY these keys are accepted, anything else is a 400: name (string, exact match), email (string, exact), type (array of prospect|client|supplier), is_archived (boolean), id (array of integer company ids; the key is `id`, not `ids`), contacts (array of integer contact ids), siret (string), vat (string), reference (array of strings), country_code (string), postal_code (array of strings), number_of_employees ({"min": n, "max": n}), favourite_filter (integer), created ({"start", "end"}), updated_at ({"start", "end"}; the key is `updated_at`, not `updated`). Dates must be full ISO 8601 date-times, e.g. {"created": {"start": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"}}; a bare date is rejected. Pass {} for no filter.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2…) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_get_company
tools.description: Read one client company in full: addresses, contacts, tax identifiers, rating and the notes recorded against it.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: invoicing_address, delivery_address, e_invoicing, main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact, opportunities, estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, acl, smart_tags, owner, or cf.<customFieldId>. Any other value (e.g. `contacts`) is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_list_contacts
tools.description: List individual contacts with their name, e-mail, phone, position and the company they belong to.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2…) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_list_invoices
tools.description: List invoices with their number, date, due date, client, net and gross totals and payment status: the receivables view.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2…) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: acl, owner, related, contact, individual, company, fiscal_year, currency, smart_tags, deposits, invoicing_address, delivery_address, issuer_address, payment_method_ids, or cf.<customFieldId>.

tools.name: sellsy_search_invoices
tools.description: Search invoices with Sellsy's filter object: by status, date range, client or amount. A POST that only reads.

filters.description: Sellsy invoice filters. Allowed keys: date ({"start", "end"} as plain dates YYYY-MM-DD, the invoice date), created / updated ({"start", "end"} as full ISO 8601 date-times, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00; a bare date is rejected), status (array of draft|due|payinprogress|paid|late|cancelled), related_objects (array of {"type": company|individual|opportunity, "id": n}), contacts, owners, assigned_staff_ids (arrays of integer ids), number (string), currency (string), credit_note_id (integer), is_deposit (boolean), is_progress_invoice (boolean), lifecycle_status (array of integer), favourite_filter (integer). Example: {"status": ["late"], "date": {"start": "2026-01-01"}}. Pass {} for no filter.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2…) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_get_invoice
tools.description: Read one invoice in full: every row with its quantity, unit price, discount and VAT, the totals and the related parties. Payments are not part of this response.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: acl, payment_terms, owner, related, contact, individual, company, fiscal_year, currency, automatic_dunning, smart_tags, discount_incl_taxes, deposits, invoicing_address, delivery_address, issuer_address, payment_method_ids, settings, file, or cf.<customFieldId>. Rows are returned without an embed.

tools.name: sellsy_list_estimates
tools.description: List estimates (devis) with their number, date, client, total and acceptance status: what is out with prospects and not yet won.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2…) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_list_opportunities
tools.description: List CRM opportunities with their name, client, amount, funnel step and expected close date: the pipeline view.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2…) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_list_items
tools.description: List catalogue items with their reference, name, unit price, VAT rate and stock tracking flag.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2…) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_get_contact
tools.description: Read one contact (person) in full: name, email and phone numbers, position, note, addresses, owner, archive state and custom fields. Read it before sellsy_edit_contact.

tools.name: sellsy_list_contact_companies
tools.description: List the companies a contact is linked to. Check this before merging, archiving or moving a contact, since one person can belong to several companies.

tools.name: sellsy_edit_contact
tools.description: Change fields of a contact. Send only the fields that change, e.g. {"email": "...", "mobile_number": "...", "position": "...", "note": "...", "is_archived": false}; the others stay as they are. Field names are those returned by sellsy_get_contact. Writes to the live CRM: confirm the change with the user first.

fields.description: The fields to change, as a JSON object.

tools.name: sellsy_edit_company
tools.description: Change fields of a company. Send only the fields that change, e.g. {"name": "..."} or {"is_archived": true} to archive it (false restores it); the others stay as they are. Field names are those returned by sellsy_get_company. Writes to the live CRM: confirm the change with the user first, one company at a time.

fields.description: The fields to change, as a JSON object.

tools.name: sellsy_create_company
tools.description: Create a company (a client, prospect or supplier). Returns the new company with its id. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

tools.name: sellsy_list_company_contacts
tools.description: List the contacts (people) linked to a company, with name, e-mail, phones, position and their roles at the company.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: invoicing_address, delivery_address, opportunities, estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proposals, proposals_ids, acl, smart_tags, owner, company, or cf.<customFieldId>. Any other value is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_link_contact_to_company
tools.description: Link an existing contact to a company, optionally with roles (e.g. ["main", "invoicing", "dunning"]). Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

roles.description: Roles of the contact at the company: main, dunning, invoicing, or a custom role id.

tools.name: sellsy_list_company_addresses
tools.description: List the addresses of a company (invoicing, delivery and others) with their ids, for use as invoicing_address_id or delivery_address_id on documents.

tools.name: sellsy_create_company_address
tools.description: Add an address to a company. The first address becomes the invoicing and delivery address unless set otherwise. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

name.description: Label of the address, e.g. "Head office".

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. FR.

tools.name: sellsy_get_company_custom_fields
tools.description: Read the custom field values of a company: field id, name, type and value. Field definitions are in sellsy_list_custom_fields.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_update_company_custom_fields
tools.description: Set custom field values on a company. Only the listed fields change. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

values.description: The values to set, e.g. [{"id": 1542, "value": "Gold"}]; id is the custom field id from sellsy_list_custom_fields.

tools.name: sellsy_list_company_files
tools.description: List the directories and files attached to a company (contracts, scans, exports), with file ids for sellsy_get_file.

tools.name: sellsy_list_individuals
tools.description: List individuals (private persons who are clients, prospects or suppliers in their own right, unlike contacts who belong to a company) with name, e-mail, phones and type.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: invoicing_address, delivery_address, main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact, opportunities, estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proposals, proposals_ids, acl, smart_tags, owner, or cf.<customFieldId>. Any other value is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_search_individuals
tools.description: Search individual with Sellsy's filter object (a POST that only reads). Only the documented filter keys are accepted; an unknown key or a bare date where a date-time is expected is a 400.

filters.description: Sellsy individual filters. Allowed keys: name (string), email (string), type (array of prospect|client|supplier), is_archived (boolean), id (array of integer ids), country_code (string), postal_code (array of strings), reference (array of strings), favourite_filter (integer), created ({"start", "end"}), updated_at ({"start", "end"}). Dates must be full ISO 8601 date-times, e.g. {"created": {"start": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"}}; a bare date is rejected. Pass {} for no filter.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_get_individual
tools.description: Read one individual in full: name, contact details, type, addresses, owner and notes.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: invoicing_address, delivery_address, main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact, opportunities, estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proposals, proposals_ids, acl, smart_tags, owner, or cf.<customFieldId>. Any other value is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_create_individual
tools.description: Create an individual (a private person as client, prospect or supplier). Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

tools.name: sellsy_edit_individual
tools.description: Change fields of an individual. Send only the fields that change, e.g. {"email": "...", "type": "client"}; field names are those of sellsy_get_individual. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

fields.description: The fields to change, as a JSON object.

tools.name: sellsy_search_contacts
tools.description: Search contact with Sellsy's filter object (a POST that only reads). Only the documented filter keys are accepted; an unknown key or a bare date where a date-time is expected is a 400.

filters.description: Sellsy contact filters. Allowed keys: last_name (string), email (string), phone_number (string), mobile_number (string), companies (array of company ids), individuals (array of individual ids), id (array of integer ids), is_linked (boolean), country_code (string), postal_code (array of strings), favourite_filter (integer), created / updated / birth_date ({"start", "end"}). Dates must be full ISO 8601 date-times, e.g. {"created": {"start": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"}}; a bare date is rejected. Pass {} for no filter.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_create_contact
tools.description: Create a contact (a person, usually working at a company). Link it to a company afterwards with sellsy_link_contact_to_company. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

tools.name: sellsy_get_opportunity
tools.description: Read one opportunity: name, status, pipeline and step, amount, probability, due date, source, related company or individual, contacts, assigned staff and note.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: estimates, individual, invoices, orders, deliveries, proformas, creditnotes, estimates_ids, invoices_ids, orders_ids, deliveries_ids, proformas_ids, creditnotes_ids, proposals, proposals_ids, assigned_staffs, company, contacts, acl, currency, smart_tags, or cf.<customFieldId>. Any other value is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_search_opportunities
tools.description: Search opportunity with Sellsy's filter object (a POST that only reads). Only the documented filter keys are accepted; an unknown key or a bare date where a date-time is expected is a 400.

filters.description: Sellsy opportunity filters. Allowed keys: name (string), number (string), statuses (array of open|won|lost|cancelled|closed|late), pipeline (array of pipeline ids), step (array of step ids), amount ({"min", "max"}), related_objects (array of {"type": company|individual, "id": n}), assigned_staffs, owners (arrays of staff ids), favourite_filter (integer), created / updated_status / due_date ({"start", "end"}). Dates must be full ISO 8601 date-times, e.g. {"created": {"start": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"}}; a bare date is rejected. Pass {} for no filter.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_create_opportunity
tools.description: Create an opportunity in a pipeline step for a company or individual. Get pipeline and step ids from sellsy_list_opportunity_pipelines and sellsy_list_pipeline_steps. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

related.description: Exactly one company or individual, plus optional contacts: [{"type": "company", "id": 123}] or [{"type": "individual", "id": 45}].

amount.description: Potential amount in the account default currency, e.g. "12000.00".

owner_id.description: Staff id of the owner (default: the API user).

assigned_staff_ids.description: Staff ids assigned to the opportunity.

contact_ids.description: Contact ids responsible on the client side.

tools.name: sellsy_update_opportunity
tools.description: Partly update an opportunity, e.g. mark it won or lost, change its amount or due date. List every field you send in only; Sellsy ignores the others. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

only.description: Names of the fields to update, e.g. ["status", "amount"].

owner_id.description: Staff id of the new owner.

tools.name: sellsy_move_opportunity_step
tools.description: Move an opportunity to another step of its pipeline (the kanban move), optionally placing it before another opportunity. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

before_sibling.description: Id of the opportunity to place it before; leave out to put it last.

tools.name: sellsy_list_opportunity_pipelines
tools.description: List the opportunity pipelines (sales funnels) with their ids and names.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_list_pipeline_steps
tools.description: List the steps of one pipeline in order, with id, name, rank and default probability. embed opportunities_number adds how many opportunities sit in each step.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: opportunities_number. Any other value is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_list_opportunity_sources
tools.description: List the opportunity sources (where leads come from: website, trade fair, referral...) with their ids.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_list_opportunity_categories
tools.description: List the categories that group opportunity sources; embed sources returns the sources of each category.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: sources. Any other value is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_get_estimate
tools.description: Read one estimate (devis) in full: number, date, expiry date, status, related parties, rows with quantity, price and VAT, totals and the PDF link.

embed.description: Related objects to return inline. Allowed values only: company, individual, contact, invoicing_address, delivery_address, issuer_address, currency, acl, payment_method_ids, fiscal_year, smart_tags, payment_terms, settings, rate_category, proposals, proposals_ids, or cf.<customFieldId>. Any other value is a 400.

tools.name: sellsy_search_estimates
tools.description: Search estimate with Sellsy's filter object (a POST that only reads). Only the documented filter keys are accepted; an unknown key or a bare date where a date-time is expected is a 400.

filters.description: Sellsy estimate filters. Allowed keys: status (array of draft|sent|read|accepted|refused|expired|advanced|partialinvoiced|invoiced|cancelled), date ({"start", "end"} as plain dates YYYY-MM-DD), created / updated ({"start", "end"} as full date-times), related_objects (array of {"type": company|individual|opportunity, "id": n}), contacts, owners, assigned_staff_ids (arrays of ids), number (string), currency (string), favourite_filter (integer). Pass {} for no filter.

offset.description: `pagination.offset` from the previous response (an opaque seek token). A plain page number (0, 1, 2...) also works, up to the first 100,000 results.

tools.name: sellsy_create_estimate
tools.description: Create an estimate (devis) as a draft. Send the document as an object; the totals are computed by Sellsy. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

document.description: The estimate. Required: related, e.g. [{"type": "company", "id": 123}] (a company, individual or opportunity; add {"type": "contact", "id": n} for the contact). Common fields: date and expiry_date (YYYY-MM-DD), subject, currency (e.g. EUR), note, assigned_staff_id, contact_id, invoicing_address_id, payment_terms ({"id": n}), rows: an array of rows, each {"type": "single", "reference": "...", "description": "...", "unit_amount": "100.00", "quantity": "2", "tax_id": n, "unit_id": n} for a free line, {"type": "catalog", "related": {"type": "product"|"service", "id": itemId}, "quantity": "1"} for a catalogue item, or {"type": "comment", "text": "..."}, {"type": "title", "text": "..."}, {"type": "sub-total"}, {"type": "break-line"}, {"type": "break-page"}.

tools.name: sellsy_update_estimate_status
tools.description: Change the status of an estimate, e.g. to accepted when the client signed or refused when they declined. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

tools.name: sellsy_create_invoice
tools.description: Create an invoice as a draft (it gets its final number when validated with sellsy_validate_invoice). Send the document as an object; the totals are computed by Sellsy. Writes to the live CRM: confirm with the user first.

document.description: The invoice. Required: related, e.g. [{"type": "company", "id": 123}] (one client company or individual, optionally a contact and opportunities).
